doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Arranging for Chick Webb, including Liza
summary: He took arrangements in hoping they would be played; he does not recall whether Webb asked for Liza.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When you joined him, was there again some understanding you would be contributing arrangements as well?

Well, I don’t know about an understanding. It might have been a tacit understanding, you know, just knowing that I could write, you know, and maybe I went into the band assuming that I would probably write if asked to do so, or that if I took something in, they would play it. In those days you didn’t always wait for someone to ask you to write it. You’d want to do something on a certain tune, and you’d make the arrangement, and you’d take it in and hope they would listen to it, and hope that if they listened to it, they’d like it, and hoped that if they’d like it, they would play it. And if they would play it, you hoped they’d play it the second time.
And that someone else would play it.

An arrangement that you did for him, like Liza, for example, which was really one of the greatest features for him as a drummer. Do you remember if he asked you to arrange that for him, or did you decide . . .
I don’t remember. It might have been something that I just thought up to do because I liked the tune at the time. It was very interesting at the time. It still is, of course.
